-- These finite equations inspect the actual prepared Core before erasure.
-- A minor must use the reconstructed current constructor, not a captured major.
def sh1CoreMajorCapture (n : Nat) : Nat :=
  match n with
  | Nat.zero => 0
  | Nat.succ predecessor =>
      Nat.add n (sh1CoreMajorCapture predecessor)

-- Nested inspection retains the established outer-child recursive hypothesis.
-- The newly inspected inner field is not a recursive-call permission.
def sh1CoreNestedOuter (n : Nat) : Nat :=
  match n with
  | Nat.zero => 0
  | Nat.succ outer =>
      match outer with
      | Nat.zero => Nat.add n (sh1CoreNestedOuter outer)
      | Nat.succ inner => Nat.add n (sh1CoreNestedOuter outer)

sourceArgument: The first new definition has the independent source equation S(0)=0 and S(k+1)=(k+1)+S(k). The second branches on k but both alternatives compute (k+1)+S(k) using only the root-established recursive call on k. Thus each has S(2)=3 and S(3)=6.

The Core reference implements Nat.rec M z s 0=z and Nat.rec M z s (k+1)=s k (Nat.rec M z s k), restricted to a syntactically constant Nat motive and proper Nat values. It applies the actual prepared minor closure, preserving its actual lexical environment. A captured original major n therefore repeats n at each fold step and yields 4/9 on inputs2/3; constructor refinement yields3/6.

bvar index0 denotes the nearest environment value. Applying an actual Core lambda extends its captured environment on the left. Core app evaluates fn, then arg, then applies; letE evaluates its initializer in the old environment, then extends the environment for its body. Neither closure environments nor minors are synthesized from expected fixture values.

The shared20,000 budget counts every runtime expression dispatch, application and Nat-rec iteration across allfour observations and recursive definition calls. Major values above64, environments beyond128, unsupported runtime forms/constants, open terms/levels, or malformed names/lists are refused. Snapshot traversal has its own8,192-node/128-depth bound and includes actual annotations.

The observed prepared declarations are selected by exact typed PsName segments, checked to have no universe parameters and exactly one explicit Nat parameter with Nat result, serialized from actual .type/.value fields, and hashed independently of admissions normalization or original-IR erasure.

This is finite value evidence over two closed total Nat programs. It does not establish general source/Core demand semantics, callback/divergence adequacy, all-input correctness, a kernel theorem, or any strict/general conformance closure.
